relevance_note: The paper describes 12 SURF patients with individually tabulated NOD2 variants and two Blau syndrome patients, e.g. 'The disease control group comprised two BS patients harboring the heterozygous R587C variant.'
method_note: Table 2 lists patients as columns (header row '| Variables | P1 | P2 | ... | P12 | BS1 | BS2 |', first header row 'SURF patients' x12 and 'Blau syndrome' x2); a Python script in the scratch directory sliced each row from its label through the patient's cell for spans, and its cell values were checked against the table by eye. 'Age, y' was recorded as age at last evaluation (Table 1 calls it current age); onset from 'Age at disease onset, y'. In scope: P1-P12 (SURF with NOD2 variants), BS1-BS2 (Blau syndrome, R587C), and HC1, a healthy control described as a heterozygous R702W carrier with an individual Western blot result (no phenotype data; checklist all not reported). HC2 (wild-type NOD2) is out of scope. P8 'P268S/V955I' and P12 'R702W/ P268S' were split into two variant rows each; their ACMG cells 'B/LB' and 'VUS/B' were assigned to the variants in the order printed within the same patient's cell (P268S alone is 'B' for P7). Zygosity: heterozygous from the sentence naming each variant; compound heterozygous for P8 and P12 from 'two patients carried compound heterozygous variants'; P4 left not reported because the heterozygous list prints 'L1000fs' while Table 2 prints 'L1007fs' and the Discussion 'L1007fsinsC'. Variant strings are protein-level short forms as printed (no p. prefix, no cDNA, no transcript); variant type not stated by the authors. Elevated CRP and SAA observed for P1-P12 from 'All patients experienced recurrent fevers accompanied by elevated CRP and SAA levels during attacks' (Results on the SURF cohort); not applied to BS1/BS2. The Discussion sentence that oral ulcers, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, pericarditis, conjunctivitis and periorbital edema 'were not detected' does not name the group, so nothing was excluded from it. Table 2 'Complication: None' cells excluded nothing specific. Table 1 group counts (e.g. consanguinity 2/12, family history 3/12) were not assigned to individuals. Contradictions in the paper: '53.8% female' in text vs Table 1 '7 (58.3%)' and 7 F in Table 2; 'Six distinct heterozygous NOD2 variants' followed by seven names; L1000fs vs L1007fs vs L1007fsinsC; Table 1 onset range 0.5-16 vs Table 2 minimum 1 and text 'ranged from 1 to 16 years'; ACMG classification cites reference (8) in one place and (12) in another.
